topic.subject: social
topic.title: What is government
topic.scope: levels of government, laws, democracy vs monarchy, universal adult franchise

misconceptions.statement: The village government is independent of the national government.
misconceptions.why: Students see the local office as the only one they interact with.
misconceptions.fix: All levels of government are connected; local bodies follow laws made at state and national levels.

probe.question: Can a village make a law that contradicts a national law?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is their village.

misconceptions.root_belief: Local events are isolated from larger systems.

misconceptions.statement: In a democracy, the government can do whatever the majority wants.
misconceptions.why: Confusion between majority rule and the protection of rights.
misconceptions.fix: Democracy protects the rights of minorities and follows a constitution, not just the majority's whim.

probe.question: If 90% of people want to ban a minority group's religion, can the government do it?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because democracy means majority rule.

misconceptions.root_belief: Majority opinion is always the correct rule.

misconceptions.statement: Monarchs in history were always cruel dictators.
misconceptions.fix: Some monarchs were benevolent and worked for the welfare of their subjects.
misconceptions.why: Pop culture and stories often portray kings as villains.

probe.question: Was every king in history a bad person?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, kings only care about themselves.

misconceptions.root_belief: Roles are defined by fixed character traits.

misconceptions.statement: Universal adult franchise means everyone in the country can vote.
misconceptions.why: Students often ignore the word 'adult' and think it means 'all people'.
misconceptions.fix: Only citizens who have reached the age of 18 or older are eligible to vote.

probe.question: Can a 10-year-old child vote in an election?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is universal franchise.

misconceptions.root_belief: A word means its everyday meaning.

misconceptions.statement: The Gram Panchayat is run by officials sent from the state capital, not chosen by villagers.
misconceptions.why: Students see government as officers appointed from above and do not know that villagers elect their own panchayat members.
misconceptions.fix: The Gram Panchayat is elected by the adults of the village (the Gram Sabha). The Sarpanch and ward members are chosen by voting.

probe.question: Who chooses the members of the Gram Panchayat?
probe.wrong_answer: The state government sends officers to run it.

misconceptions.root_belief: Local government is appointed from above, not elected

misconceptions.statement: The Gram Panchayat only handles village festivals and has no real responsibilities.
misconceptions.why: Students see local government as ceremonial and only notice visible events in the village.
misconceptions.fix: The Gram Panchayat looks after village roads, drinking water, street lights, sanitation and schools, and collects local taxes.

probe.question: Name one job of the Gram Panchayat.
probe.wrong_answer: Organising the village fair; it does not do anything else.

misconceptions.root_belief: Local government has trivial, limited functions

misconceptions.statement: The State Government makes the laws for the whole country.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up the State and the Centre because both are called government and both make laws.
misconceptions.fix: The State Government makes laws and decisions for its own state on subjects such as police, farming and local administration. Laws for the whole country are made by the Central Government.

probe.question: Who makes the laws that apply to all states of India?
probe.wrong_answer: The State Government of each state.

misconceptions.root_belief: State and national governments have the same reach

misconceptions.statement: The Central Government only works in Delhi and looks after only Delhi.
misconceptions.why: Students link the Central Government to its location in the capital and think its work is limited there.
misconceptions.fix: The Central Government sits in Delhi but makes decisions for the whole country, such as defence, currency, railways and foreign affairs.

probe.question: Which area does the Central Government look after?

misconceptions.root_belief: Government's work is limited to where its office is

misconceptions.statement: People take part in government only by voting, and nothing else counts.
misconceptions.why: Voting is the most visible form of participation, so students think it is the only one.
misconceptions.fix: People also take part by attending Gram Sabha meetings, giving suggestions, paying taxes, and asking officials questions or raising problems.

probe.question: How can a villager take part in government between elections?
probe.wrong_answer: They cannot; they can only vote once in five years.

misconceptions.statement: A king could be punished or removed by the people if they disliked the decisions.
misconceptions.why: Students carry the idea of democratic accountability into monarchy.
misconceptions.fix: In a monarchy the king or queen holds power by birth, and the position passes down in the family. Ordinary people had no legal way to remove them.

probe.question: How was a monarch chosen and changed in a monarchy?
probe.wrong_answer: People voted to choose or replace the king.

misconceptions.root_belief: All rulers are accountable to voters

misconceptions.statement: The right to vote depends on how much money or education a person has.
misconceptions.why: Students hear that rich or educated people are important and assume they alone get a say.
misconceptions.fix: Every adult citizen can vote regardless of wealth, education, religion, caste or gender. This is the equal right to vote.

probe.question: Can a poor villager who never went to school vote in India?
probe.wrong_answer: No, only educated or rich people can vote.

misconceptions.root_belief: Wealth or education decides political rights

misconceptions.statement: A monarchy and a democracy are the same, since in both someone rules the country.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on 'someone rules' and ignore how the ruler comes to power.
misconceptions.fix: In a democracy the people elect their leaders for a fixed time. In a monarchy the ruler gets power by birth and often rules for life.

probe.question: What is the main difference between a monarchy and a democracy?
probe.wrong_answer: There is no difference; in both a leader rules the country.

misconceptions.root_belief: All governments work the same way
